functionalObligations.text: each perpetual market runs an independent price-time-priority order book, and the Clearinghouse holds per-trader margin balances and open positions as the chain's core execution component
functionalObligations.note: Ob names the book. Note this is an in-consensus book: the corpus marker calling Ob 'only approximately applies — matching is engine-side with on-chain settlement, not an on-chain book' is STALE and is dropped (see F2).

functionalObligations.text: all order matching and trading logic are processed and stored on-chain, inside Aster Chain — the venue's own Layer 1, launched 16 March 2026, running Proof-of-Staked-Authority consensus at 50 ms blocks with zero gas
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE — matching locus, and a DEPARTURE from the corpus, which groups Aster with the operator-run books. Its own documentation puts it on Hyperliquid's side of the split. This also refutes the corpus's three-model taxonomy: Aster is a FOURTH model — in-consensus, but with a closed validator set and closed-source node software (F3) — which has the failure modes of an operator behind the surface of a chain. Launch date corroborated at https://docs.asterdex.com/llms-full.txt (2026-08-04).

functionalObligations.text: external validator participation is not supported in Phase 1, and core chain contracts and RPC infrastructure are not open-sourced, as stated policy, in order to protect proprietary matching engine algorithms
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE — operator discretion. The set that matches, prices, signs the bridge and votes on listings is closed and its software is secret. Nothing in the vocabulary can record 'the execution rule is secret while the state commitment is public', which is precisely the trust argument the venue makes.

functionalObligations.text: no validity or fraud proof covers execution; safety rests on a permissioned PoSA validator set, while zero-knowledge verification is applied at the order layer — every hidden order requires ZK verification whether or not Account Privacy is enabled
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE — proof system. The 58 have no element for a proof at all, so they cannot record that this venue proves ORDER CONFIDENTIALITY rather than STATE VALIDITY — the inverse of every other venue in the lane. No audit of Aster Chain, the clearinghouse, the matching engine or the ZK privacy stack is published (https://docs.asterdex.com/overview/audit-reports.md, 2026-08-04).

functionalObligations.text: data storage is hybrid: key trading and account events are recorded on chain while certain operations remain off chain for privacy protection and system efficiency
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE — data availability. Which operations are withheld is not enumerated, so the reconstructibility of the venue's state from public data is unknown. Compare Lighter's sufficiency predicate ('enough to reconstruct every account'), which is the same design question answered precisely.

functionalObligations.text: there is no forced-inclusion path, censorship deadline or escape hatch: withdrawals are batched and paid on 2-of-3 validator confirmation, typically in about 30 seconds, with a fee covering validator operating costs
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE — exit. Exit is entirely at the discretion of a closed 4-node set; the vocabulary can name neither the mechanism nor its absence.

functionalObligations.text: collateral is bridged in from BNB Chain, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Solana or SUI and credited once 3 of 4 validator nodes verify the deposit, at zero deposit fee, in 1 to 5 minutes
functionalObligations.note: Xm is ADDED relative to the corpus, which lists Xf alone: the bridge is validator-signed and on-chain-verifiable on explicit 3-of-4 and 2-of-3 thresholds (https://docs.asterdex.com/aster-chain/overview.md, 2026-08-04). What neither symbol carries is that the bridge's signer set is the same committee that matches orders and publishes prices.

functionalObligations.text: initial margin is position size times mark price divided by leverage, maintenance margin is tiered by position size, collateral is cross by default with per-position isolated margin and a multi-asset mode letting several tokens back one book
functionalObligations.note: Ct computes the test; margin scope (cross / isolated / multi-asset) remains unnameable, as it does across the category.

functionalObligations.text: margin may be posted in yield-bearing instruments — asBNB, USDF, asUSDF, asBTC and asCAKE — each of which is a claim on another protocol's strategy with its own minter contract, its own peg and its own auditor
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Nothing names 'collateral that is itself a position in another protocol', so the margin engine's exposure to an exogenous strategy is invisible. The corpus's candidate `Dp` describes the USDF issuer's hedge, not Aster's obligation. Audits cover these collateral products (Salus, PeckShield, HALBORN) and NOT the venue (https://docs.asterdex.com/overview/audit-reports.md, 2026-08-04).

functionalObligations.text: positions are marked to the median of the index adjusted by funding over the remaining interval, the index plus a 5-minute moving average of the mid-index basis, and the contract price, with exchanges deviating more than 5% from the median down-weighted, feeds staler than 3 seconds dropped, and a contract price more than 5% from mark replaced if not refreshed within 5 seconds
functionalObligations.note: Tp discharges the 5-minute moving-average component; Ex the external legs. The staleness and deviation guards are the freshness validation that L13 demands of Ex, and are stated here as explicit numbers that the symbol cannot carry.

functionalObligations.text: each validator computes a weighted median spot price over 14 named exchanges, and liquidation uses the median oracle price weighted by validator stake
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and a DEPARTURE: the corpus lists Ex as merely derived for Aster while raising endogenous-oracle residue for Hyperliquid, whose construction here is structurally identical. Ex names an EXTERNAL publisher; the publisher is the chain's own closed validator set, which is the opposite trust argument.

functionalObligations.text: the 1001x venue prices from Pyth as anchor, cross-verified against Chainlink by the smart contract at trade time, with Binance Oracle as fallback where Pyth lacks a pair, and a circuit breaker on more than 1% divergence
functionalObligations.note: Here Ex fits without qualification — genuinely external publishers, cross-verified on chain. One venue therefore runs an endogenous oracle and an exogenous one side by side, and the same symbol covers both.

functionalObligations.text: longs and shorts exchange funding on a default 8-hour interval at F = [P + clamp(interest - P, -0.05%, +0.05%)] / (8/N), with interest 0.01% (0% for BNBUSDT) and the premium index recomputed every 5 seconds; on Shield Mode the same transfer is generated hourly from the long/short open-interest imbalance, clamped between a floor and a cap
functionalObligations.note: Pf fits exactly on BOTH venues — the category's 'perp tether' flag is refuted here, including on the pool venue, which balances long/short interest by transfer rather than charging a utilisation borrow fee (https://docs.asterdex.com/trading/shield-mode/funding-fee-rate.md, 2026-08-04).

functionalObligations.text: the venue reserves the right to change the funding floor, the cap and the settlement interval under volatile market conditions
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER and APPROXIMATE. Sv is 'servicing & determination discretion', drawn from credit servicing; used here for a unilateral right to redetermine the parameters of the tether itself. It is the only element in the 58 that names discretion over a contract's cash flows, and it is warranted (Sh present). Recorded rather than dropped because this is the one place in the lane where an operator's discretion IS documented and therefore checkable.

functionalObligations.text: a position is liquidated when initial collateral plus realised plus unrealised PnL falls below maintenance margin, evaluated against the stake-weighted median oracle price, with an IOC close attempted first and an Insurance Clearance Fee taken
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE for Li — the engine attempts the close and charges a fee to the insurance fund; no third-party keeper is paid. Li is retained because a genuine forced close against the book occurs.

functionalObligations.text: any residue that the IOC attempt cannot close is taken over at the bankruptcy price by the insurance fund, which covers the shortfall where it can
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE — Bs is 'slashable first-loss capital'. This fund IS first-loss and IS dedicated to the waterfall, which is why it is retained here and NOT for ApeX or edgeX, but it is fee-funded protocol reserve rather than a slashable bond, so the staking half is absent. This is the category residue the corpus already names ('insurance funds as a thing distinct from slashable backstops'), instantiated. Corroborated at https://docs.asterdex.com/llms-full.txt (2026-08-04).

functionalObligations.text: when the insurance fund cannot cover the shortfall, profitable opposite-side positions are reduced, ranked by PnL% times effective leverage for winners and PnL% divided by effective leverage for losers, with a four-bar LeveragePnLQuantile indicator exposing a trader's queue position
functionalObligations.note: Ad is ADDED relative to the corpus, whose Aster element set contains no loss-absorption element at all and is therefore rejected by the requirement tables (satisfiesRequirementsAndWarrants: false). Aster documents TWO — the insurance fund (F16) and ADL — and the corpus records neither.

functionalObligations.text: on Shield Mode and 1001x the trader's counterparty is the ALP pool at an oracle price, with no order book and no inventory-repricing curve; risk is managed by fees, caps and a liquidation loss rate rather than by a curve
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the reason `Pm` is DROPPED from the corpus element set. Pm is an oracle-priced INVENTORY CURVE; stage 1 establishes there is no curve at all, so the 'proactive market making' half is not approximate but absent. Zero-slippage oracle execution as an execution property has no symbol — the same gap the corpus records for Jupiter.

functionalObligations.text: ALP holders are the market-maker counterparty for pool-venue perp trades, and NAV accrues trading PnL on that flow, protocol trading fees, funding fees, liquidation profits and platform fees rather than distributing them
functionalObligations.note: Sh names the pro-rata NAV claim. It does not name that the claim is structurally SHORT aggregate trader profit — the dominant risk of holding it. ALP is mintable on BNB Chain and Arbitrum, so the claim exists on domains other than the venue's own chain.

functionalObligations.text: Shield Mode liquidation triggers on last price against a liquidation price derived from margin, leverage, entry, funding and a liquidation loss rate that varies by pair and leverage band (BTC/ETH 75% at 1-200x, 70% at 201-500x, 65% at 501-1001x), and the 1001x venue charges no opening fee, permits no margin top-up, charges a dynamic PnL-based closing fee and caps net ROI at roughly 300%
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Two unnameable objects: a haircut applied AT liquidation that is distinct from both maintenance margin and the liquidation fee; and a payoff transformation as a venue parameter — a capped, fee-deformed perp is closer to Op than to Pf and no symbol composes 'perp with truncated upside'. Leverage terms at https://docs.asterdex.com/trading/1001x/leverage.md (2026-08-04).

functionalObligations.text: with Account Privacy enabled a trader's balances and open positions are hidden behind encrypted state, and internal transfers to other users are blocked while it is active
functionalObligations.note: Sb (shielded-balance state) fits the balance half and is exercised here for the first time in the corpus — the vocabulary note records Sb as unused by all 72 corpus decompositions. It does not carry the fact that enabling privacy disables a different function (staking requires privacy off).

functionalObligations.text: a hidden order reveals neither size nor presence to the public book while sharing the book's liquidity, always carries ZK verification of order data whether or not Account Privacy is on, and produces hidden positions excluded from all public data and portfolio analytics; a fresh one-time stealth address is generated per trade so that activity cannot be correlated
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Sb is a shielded BALANCE, not a shielded resting ORDER, and nothing reaches per-trade stealth addressing. Sharper than the corpus records: privacy is MANDATORY at the order layer and OPTIONAL at the account layer — two privacy scopes with opposite defaults. The chain-level cryptography is documented at https://docs.asterdex.com/aster-chain/overview.md while the product page describes no cryptography at all, a seam recorded here rather than resolved.

functionalObligations.text: a trader may disclose their own trading history, or another trader's if supplied with that trader's viewer pass, without lifting privacy generally
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER and APPROXIMATE. Sd is a selective-disclosure proof about oneself; the viewer pass also releases ANOTHER party's history on presentation of a bearer capability, which is an auditability instrument rather than a proof. Like Sb, first use in the corpus.

functionalObligations.text: ASTER is staked to validators with a lock period and an early-exit path, rewards split into a Base APY pool allocated by each validator's share of processed transactions and Loyalty Rewards weighted by lock length through veASTER, and Account Privacy must be off to stake
functionalObligations.note: Vl is ADDED relative to the corpus (CANDIDATE-REGISTER); Em covers the Base APY pool. Vl names a lifecycle, not the role bundle: this same set is matcher, oracle publisher, bridge signer and listing electorate.

functionalObligations.text: listing is decided by validator vote: any active validator holding at least 20M staked ASTER may propose, and passage requires a double majority of more than 50% of stake and more than 50% of validators, formalised as AOS-1 for spot listing since 25 June 2026
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. A listing franchise attached to consensus participation, decided by a double majority, is neither Vl (a lifecycle) nor Aw (an identity gate). Compare Hyperliquid, which prices the same right by Dutch auction: two venues answer the same design question with mechanisms the vocabulary cannot distinguish because it names neither.

functionalObligations.text: no timelock, guardian, pause authority or upgrade path for the chain or its contracts is documented
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the reason `Gp` and `Up` are DROPPED from the corpus element set. Stage 1 searched the documentation corpus and found none; asserting a guardian or a mutable proxy on a closed-source chain with no published contracts would be a claim from memory, which the run's invariants forbid.
